judged_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51-60 — `addMembers()`'s ajax `.then` has no `.catch`; if the PUT to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` fails (e.g. validation error triggers `render_json_error` in the controller), the rejection is unhandled and the `admin-group.js.es6:61-65` caller (`this.get("model").addMembers(...)`) never surfaces any error or clears/restores the input, so the admin sees no feedback that adding members failed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Discourse.Group#addMembers` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function(){ self.findMembers(); })` with no local error handling, and the new `admin-group.js.es6` `addMembers` action calls `this.get('model').addMembers(this.get('usernames'))` without chaining `.then/.catch` or otherwise surfacing failures/clearing the input. From the diff alone, it’s verifiable that this path provides no explicit feedback on request failure (unlike the `save` action which has a `.catch(showModal...)`). Whether the rejection is truly “unhandled” depends on `Discourse.ajax` global behavior, which isn’t shown here, so this is a concrete UX/robustness concern rather than a definitively broken bug.
